text: In the cumene to phenol preparation in presence of air, the intermediate is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

With dilute acid, the phenyl group of cumene hydroperoxide migrates from carbon to oxygen, and hydrolysis gives phenol and acetone.


[IMG]

Option (A) is cumene itself, (B) is isopropyl phenyl ether and (C) is phenyl acetate; none of these is formed in the process.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The correct order in aqueous medium of basic strength in case of methyl substituted amines is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the gas phase only the $+I$ effect of the methyl groups operates, giving $\mathrm{Me}{}_{3}\mathrm{N}>\mathrm{Me}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}>\mathrm{MeNH}{}_{2}>\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ (option (B)), but this order does not hold in water.

In water the protonated amine is also stabilised by hydrogen bonding with water molecules; the more $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds the cation has, the better it is solvated.

$\mathrm{Me}{}_{3}\mathrm{NH}{}^{+}$ has only one $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ bond and its three methyl groups hinder solvation, so trimethylamine falls below methylamine despite the larger $+I$ effect.

The combined $+I$, solvation and steric effects give the aqueous order (pKb in brackets):

$\mathrm{Me}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}(3.27)>\mathrm{MeNH}{}_{2}(3.38)>\mathrm{Me}{}_{3}\mathrm{N}(4.22)>\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}(4.75)$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text:
Match the List-I with List-II :

  
    
    List-I
Cations
    
    List-II
Group reagents
  

  
    A.
    $\mathrm{Pb}^{2+},\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$
    i)
    $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ gas in presence of dilute HCl
  
  
    B.
    $\mathrm{Al}^{3+},\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$
    ii)
    $(\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{CO}_{3}$ in presence of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$
  
  
    C.
    $\mathrm{Co}^{2+},\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$
    iii)
    $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ in presence of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$
  
  
    D.
    $\mathrm{Ba}^{2+},\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$
    iv)
    $H_{2}S$ in presence of $NH_{4}OH$
  

Correct match is -
options: A $\to$ i, B $\to$ iii, C $\to$ iv, D $\to$ ii
A $\to$ i, B $\to$ iii, C $\to$ ii, D $\to$ iv
A $\to$ iii, B $\to$ i, C $\to$ iv, D $\to$ ii
A $\to$ iv, B $\to$ ii, C $\to$ iii, D $\to$ i
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In qualitative analysis, cations are separated into analytical groups (not periodic-table groups) by group reagents.

$\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ (group II): their sulphides have very low $K_{sp}$, so they precipitate with $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ even in dilute HCl, where $[\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}]$ is kept low: i.

$\mathrm{Al}{}^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ (group III): precipitated as hydroxides by $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$, which suppresses $[\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}]$ so that only these low-$K_{sp}$ hydroxides form: iii.

$\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ (group IV): their sulphides have higher $K_{sp}$ and precipitate with $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ only in ammoniacal medium, where $[\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}]$ is high: iv.

$\mathrm{Ba}{}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Ca}{}^{2+}$ (group V): precipitated as carbonates by $(\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$: ii.

So A $\to$ i, B $\to$ iii, C $\to$ iv, D $\to$ ii.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text:
The osmotic pressure of solutions of PVC in cyclohexanone at 300 K are plotted on the graph.

The molar mass of PVC is $____________ g$ mol${}^{-1}$ (Nearest integer)


[IMG]


(Given : R = 0.083 L atm K${}^{-1}$ mol${}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the graph, $π$ varies linearly with C (in g L${}^{-1}$).

$\begin{array}{l} π=CRT \\  \\ \Rightarrow π=\dfrac{\text{mole}}{\text{volume}}\times RT \\  \\ \Rightarrow π=\dfrac{\text{mole}}{\text{volume}}\times \dfrac{\mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{M}}\times \mathrm{RT} \\  \\ \Rightarrow π=\dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}\times \dfrac{\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow π(\mathrm{atm})=\dfrac{RT}{M}\times C\left (\mathrm{g}\mathrm{lit}^{-1}\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{So, Slope}=\dfrac{\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}=\dfrac{0.083\times 300}{\mathrm{M}}=6\times 10^{-4} \\  \\ \therefore \mathrm{M}=\dfrac{0.083\times 300}{6\times 10^{-4}}=\dfrac{830\times 300}{6} \\  \\ =41,500\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mole} \end{array}$

Note: the graph in the original paper labelled the y-axis $\frac{π}{\mathrm{C}}$, which would give a horizontal line. It is shown here as $π$, which matches the official answer.

text:
The number of paramagnetic species from the following is $_____________$.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}],[\mathrm{NiC}\mathrm{l}_{4}]^{2-}$

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-},[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{N}\mathrm{H}_{3})_{4}]^{2+}$

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}\mathrm{and}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A species is paramagnetic when the metal has at least one unpaired electron in the complex.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the electrons and gives square planar $dsp^{2}$ bonding, so there are 0 unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$: Ni(0) is $3d^{8}4s^{2}$; CO pushes the $4s$ electrons into $3d$ to give $3d^{10}$ with $sp^{3}$ bonding, so there are 0 unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

$[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ gives a tetrahedral $e^{4}t_{2}^{4}$ complex with 2 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{6}$; with strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ it is low spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ with 0 unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{9}$, which always leaves 1 unpaired electron (paramagnetic).

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$; low spin $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$ leaves 1 unpaired electron (paramagnetic).

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{6}$; weak-field $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ gives high spin $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$ with 4 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

The paramagnetic species are $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$, $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}$, $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$.

Hence, the answer is 4.

For the first order reaction A $\to$ B, the half life is 30 min. The time taken for 75% completion of the reaction is $_________ \min . ($Nearest integer)

Given : log 2 = 0.3010

log 3 = 0.4771

log 5 = 0.6989
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Time taken for $75%$ completion

$=2\times \mathrm{t}_{1/2}$

$=2\times 30$

$=60\min$
